overall: The AG declined to review most allegations as untimely, unspecific, or not violations even if true, and found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on the one reviewed allegation about posting notice.

allegations.summary: First complaint alleged the notice for the December 15, 2021 meeting was insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: All three notices were for open session meetings; therefore, any deficiencies with respect to the notices were reasonably discoverable on the date each meeting occurred.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the notices for the September 2, 2021 and January 26, 2022 meetings were insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaints were filed more than 30 days after the meetings occurred, we find these allegations to be untimely and decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaints implicitly challenged generic notice topics such as 'Covid-19 Updates' and 'New Business anticipated by Chair'; the AG reminded the Board of the specificity requirement.
allegations.key_passage: lack the specificity necessary to comply with the Open Meeting Law as they do not reasonably inform the public of the anticipated nature of the topics to be discussed.

allegations.summary: First complaint alleged members of the public were not allowed to comment at the December 15, 2021 meeting; the allegation was also untimely.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation, but rather gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide whether to permit public comment during a meeting.

allegations.summary: First complaint alleged the Board considered limiting public comment and requiring names and addresses of commenters.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even assuming the allegations raised are true, they would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the minutes for several Board meetings from September 2021 to January 2022 were insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Because the second complaint was filed more than 30 days after the last set of meeting minutes was approved in open session, we find the complaint to be untimely with respect to the allegations that the minutes are insufficient.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the Board communicates via private internet chat during meetings, so information is not visible to the public, citing remote technology rules.
allegations.key_passage: Where the complaint does not identify any particular meeting during which the Board is alleged to have communicated via chat, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: First complaint alleged the January 6, 2022 meeting notice was posted at Lee town hall but not on the Board's website as customary.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it posted notice for its January 6, 2022, meeting at the town hall of each member town—Lee, Lenox, and Stockbridge—but did not also post notice on its website.
